label: Civil cases filed (IDB)
description: Civil cases filed in the district during the fiscal year, from the FJC Integrated Database.
caveats: Filing cohort: cases are counted in the federal fiscal year (Oct 1-Sep 30) of the AO's 'filing date used' (FDATEUSE), once per case (duplicate termination records of the same case are collapsed). Includes original filings, removals, transfers in, MDL transfers in, remands and reopenings, as the AO counts civil filings. Reconstructed from case records still in the cumulative file (closed or pending), so it can differ slightly from the AO's published count for the year (Judicial Business Table C-1); see reconciliation.csv. Mass-tort MDL filings make some district-years spike (e.g. N.D. Fla.: 204,990 filings in FY2020, 202,838 of them NOS 365 product liability, almost all under MDL docket 2885). FY2026 includes 80,415 NOS 463 alien-detainee habeas petitions (2,315 in FY2025).

label: Civil cases terminated (IDB)
description: Civil case terminations in the district during the fiscal year.
caveats: Termination cohort: every termination record counted in the fiscal year of the AO's 'termination date used' (TDATEUSE), as the AO counts terminations (a case closed twice counts twice). Matches the AO's published terminations (Table C-1) exactly in most years.

label: Patent cases filed (NOS 830)
description: Civil cases filed with nature of suit 830 (Patent).
caveats: Filing cohort: cases are counted in the federal fiscal year (Oct 1-Sep 30) of the AO's 'filing date used' (FDATEUSE), once per case (duplicate termination records of the same case are collapsed). Includes original filings, removals, transfers in, MDL transfers in, remands and reopenings, as the AO counts civil filings. SERIES BREAK FY2017: the AO added NOS 835 'Patent - Abbreviated New Drug Application' (Hatch-Waxman pharmaceutical cases), first used for filings in FY2017; those cases were coded 830 before and are excluded from this variable after. The break matters most in D. Del. and D.N.J.; use idb_patent_incl_anda_filed for a continuous series.

label: Patent cases filed, incl. ANDA (NOS 830 + 835)
description: Civil cases filed with nature of suit 830 (Patent) or 835 (Patent - Abbreviated New Drug Application).
caveats: Filing cohort: cases are counted in the federal fiscal year (Oct 1-Sep 30) of the AO's 'filing date used' (FDATEUSE), once per case (duplicate termination records of the same case are collapsed). Includes original filings, removals, transfers in, MDL transfers in, remands and reopenings, as the AO counts civil filings. Continuous across the FY2017 introduction of NOS 835.

label: Share of U.S. patent filings (NOS 830)
description: The district's share of all NOS 830 patent cases filed in U.S. district courts that fiscal year.
caveats: Derived. Same NOS 830 series break in FY2017 as idb_patent_filed (ANDA cases moved to NOS 835).
higher_means: larger share of the nation's patent suits
formula: 100 * idb_patent_filed[district, FY] / sum over all 94 districts of idb_patent_filed[FY]

label: Civil cases with a pro se party
description: Share of civil cases filed in which at least one party is self-represented: one or more pro se plaintiffs, one or more pro se defendants, or both (codebook PROSE codes 1, 2, 3), among cases with a reported PROSE code (0-3).
caveats: Filing cohort: cases are counted in the federal fiscal year (Oct 1-Sep 30) of the AO's 'filing date used' (FDATEUSE), once per case (duplicate termination records of the same case are collapsed). Includes original filings, removals, transfers in, MDL transfers in, remands and reopenings, as the AO counts civil filings. PROSE is the value on the case's latest record (it can change during a case) and has no AO quality control (FJC IDB Research Guide). It is blank on every record of tape years 1988-1995 and 1998, so the series starts with FY1999 filings; district-years where fewer than 95% of filings carry a PROSE code are omitted. Most pro se cases are prisoner petitions and pro se plaintiffs. Mass-tort MDL dockets can carry pro se codes on very many cases: in N.D. Fla., 110,916 of 204,990 FY2020 filings and 23,884 of 25,251 FY2024 filings have a pro se code, almost all in MDL docket 2885, which lifts that district and the national value in FY2020-21 and FY2024. Shares for districts with few cases (see the `denominator` column) are volatile.
higher_means: more cases with a self-represented party
formula: 100 * filed cases with PROSE in {1,2,3} / filed cases with PROSE in {0,1,2,3}

label: Civil cases with a pro se plaintiff
description: Share of civil cases filed with one or more self-represented plaintiffs (PROSE codes 1 and 3), among cases with a reported PROSE code.
caveats: Same coverage rules and caveats as idb_civil_pct_pro_se. Shares for districts with few cases (see the `denominator` column) are volatile.
higher_means: more cases brought by self-represented plaintiffs
formula: 100 * filed cases with PROSE in {1,3} / filed cases with PROSE in {0,1,2,3}

label: Prisoner petitions, share of civil filings
description: Share of civil cases filed that are prisoner petitions: nature of suit 510 (motion to vacate sentence), 530 (habeas corpus), 535 (death-penalty habeas), 540 (mandamus and other), 550 (prisoner civil rights), 555 (prison condition) and 560 (civil detainee).
caveats: Filing cohort: cases are counted in the federal fiscal year (Oct 1-Sep 30) of the AO's 'filing date used' (FDATEUSE), once per case (duplicate termination records of the same case are collapsed). Includes original filings, removals, transfers in, MDL transfers in, remands and reopenings, as the AO counts civil filings. Excludes NOS 463 (alien detainee habeas), which the current JS 44 also lists under 'Prisoner Petitions' but which is not in the codebook's 510-560 prisoner block; it is in the NOS mix table. Districts with federal prisons or many state prisons show high values. Shares for districts with few cases (see the `denominator` column) are volatile.
higher_means: more of the civil docket is prisoner litigation
formula: 100 * filed cases with NOS in 510-560 / all filed cases

label: Civil cases filed as class actions
description: Share of civil cases filed in which the plaintiff alleged a Rule 23 class action (CLASSACT = 1).
caveats: Filing cohort: cases are counted in the federal fiscal year (Oct 1-Sep 30) of the AO's 'filing date used' (FDATEUSE), once per case (duplicate termination records of the same case are collapsed). Includes original filings, removals, transfers in, MDL transfers in, remands and reopenings, as the AO counts civil filings. The field records the allegation at filing, not certification. Only '1' or missing (-8) occur, so 'no class allegation' and 'not reported' cannot be told apart; the FJC notes the field has no quality-control checks. Low values before about FY2001 may partly reflect reporting. Shares for districts with few cases (see the `denominator` column) are volatile.
formula: 100 * filed cases with CLASSACT = 1 / all filed cases

label: Civil terminations by trial verdict
description: Share of civil terminations disposed of by a judgment after trial: jury verdict (DISP 7), directed verdict (DISP 8) or court (bench) trial (DISP 9).
caveats: Termination cohort: every termination record counted in the fiscal year of the AO's 'termination date used' (TDATEUSE), as the AO counts terminations (a case closed twice counts twice). Counts only cases whose final disposition is a trial judgment; cases that settle or are otherwise resolved during or after a trial are not counted (see idb_civil_pct_reached_trial, the AO's 'reaching trial' measure). FY2007: M.D. La. recorded 6,350 terminations coded as jury verdicts (6,305 of them NOS 360 'other personal injury', nearly all dated May 2007), which lifts that district-year and the national value. Shares for districts with few cases (see the `denominator` column) are volatile.
higher_means: more civil cases decided by trial
formula: 100 * terminations with DISP in {7,8,9} / all terminations

label: Civil terminations during or after trial
description: Share of civil terminations whose procedural progress at disposition was during or after a court or jury trial (PROCPROG 6-9), whatever the final disposition. This is the AO's 'percent reaching trial' (Judicial Business Table C-4).
caveats: Termination cohort: every termination record counted in the fiscal year of the AO's 'termination date used' (TDATEUSE), as the AO counts terminations (a case closed twice counts twice). AO Table C-4 excludes a few hundred records a year (its total is slightly below C-1's), so national values differ from the published percent in the second decimal. Shares for districts with few cases (see the `denominator` column) are volatile.
formula: 100 * terminations with PROCPROG in {6,7,8,9} / all terminations

label: Criminal defendants filed (IDB)
description: Criminal defendants whose proceedings commenced in the district during the fiscal year (felony, Class A misdemeanor, and petty-offense defendants assigned to district judges).
caveats: Defendant-level. Counted from the FJC fiscal-year snapshot of the year with the AO's count flags; excludes inter-district (Rule 20/21) transfers so no defendant is counted in two districts. Equals the AO's Judicial Business Table D-2 total (defendants commenced, excluding transfers). Not comparable with FCMS 'felony filings' (felony only; FY2004-09 and FY2011 count cases).

label: Felony defendants filed (IDB)
description: Criminal defendants filed whose most serious filing offense is a felony (FOFFLVL1 = 4).
caveats: Defendant-level. Counted from the FJC fiscal-year snapshot of the year with the AO's count flags; excludes inter-district (Rule 20/21) transfers so no defendant is counted in two districts. Comparable with FCMS 'Total Criminal' felony filings in the years FCMS counts defendants (FY2010, FY2012+).

label: Criminal defendants terminated (IDB)
description: Criminal defendants whose cases closed in the district during the fiscal year (by dismissal, acquittal or sentencing after conviction).
caveats: Defendant-level. Counted from the FJC fiscal-year snapshot of the year with the AO's count flags; excludes inter-district (Rule 20/21) transfers so no defendant is counted in two districts. Equals AO Judicial Business Table D-4 'total defendants'.

label: Criminal defendants disposed of by trial
description: Share of terminated defendants whose final disposition followed a bench or jury trial: acquitted or convicted by the court or by a jury, including insanity verdicts (DISP1 2, 3, 8, 9, 16, 17, 18, 19).
caveats: Defendant-level. Counted from the FJC fiscal-year snapshot of the year with the AO's count flags; excludes inter-district (Rule 20/21) transfers so no defendant is counted in two districts. Same grouping as AO Table D-4's bench-trial and jury-trial columns. Mistrials (DISP1 13) are counted with dismissals, as in D-4. Shares for districts with few cases (see the `denominator` column) are volatile.
formula: 100 * terminated defendants with DISP1 in {2,3,8,9,16,17,18,19} / all terminated defendants

label: Criminal defendants convicted by guilty plea
description: Share of terminated defendants convicted on a plea of guilty or nolo contendere (DISP1 4, 5).
caveats: Defendant-level. Counted from the FJC fiscal-year snapshot of the year with the AO's count flags; excludes inter-district (Rule 20/21) transfers so no defendant is counted in two districts. Same as AO Table D-4 'plea of guilty' (which includes nolo contendere pleas). Shares for districts with few cases (see the `denominator` column) are volatile.
formula: 100 * terminated defendants with DISP1 in {4,5} / all terminated defendants

label: Criminal defendants dismissed
description: Share of terminated defendants not convicted and not acquitted: dismissed (with or without prejudice), nolle prosequi, pretrial diversion, mistrial, statistically closed, dismissal superseded (DISP1 1, 10-15, 20, 21).
caveats: Defendant-level. Counted from the FJC fiscal-year snapshot of the year with the AO's count flags; excludes inter-district (Rule 20/21) transfers so no defendant is counted in two districts. Same as AO Table D-4 'dismissed'. Includes dismissals because charges were superseded or refiled. Shares for districts with few cases (see the `denominator` column) are volatile.
formula: 100 * terminated defendants with DISP1 in {1,10,11,12,13,14,15,20,21} / all terminated defendants

label: Criminal defendants acquitted
description: Share of terminated defendants acquitted by the court or by a jury, including not guilty by reason of insanity (DISP1 2, 3, 16, 18).
caveats: Defendant-level. Counted from the FJC fiscal-year snapshot of the year with the AO's count flags; excludes inter-district (Rule 20/21) transfers so no defendant is counted in two districts. Code 2 also covers a judgment of acquittal on the defendant's motion or the court's initiative. Values are small (national ~0.2-1%). Shares for districts with few cases (see the `denominator` column) are volatile.
formula: 100 * terminated defendants with DISP1 in {2,3,16,18} / all terminated defendants

label: Immigration offenses, share of criminal defendants filed
description: Share of criminal defendants filed whose most serious filing offense (D2FOFFCD1) is in the 'immigration' category: D2 codes 8710-8750 (illegal entry, illegal re-entry, alien smuggling, visa fraud) and 9740.
caveats: Defendant-level. Counted from the FJC fiscal-year snapshot of the year with the AO's count flags; excludes inter-district (Rule 20/21) transfers so no defendant is counted in two districts. Offense categories follow AO Judicial Business Table D-2's headings; the code-to-category mapping is this lane's (pipeline/idb/codes.py), checked against the D-2 national totals for every year FY2005-2025 (offense_mapping_check.csv). D2 codes were created in FY2005 and back-filled by the FJC for FY1996-2004. Shares for districts with few cases (see the `denominator` column) are volatile.
higher_means: more of the criminal docket is immigration prosecutions
formula: 100 * defendants filed with offense category immigration / all defendants filed
